scope: Algorithm literacy is broad; GPU execution is restricted to methods that answer a diagnosed StudyHub failure.
evidence_rule: LITERATURE_ONLY and upstream support are not StudyHub run evidence. Promotion requires a versioned implementation, equal-budget comparison, independent evaluation and an artifact-backed decision.
fair_comparison_contract: branch from the same identified 9B checkpoint
use the same task distribution, environment, reward and evaluator versions
match generated tokens, optimizer updates and GPU-hours or report all three
report at least two seeds for a promotion claim and three when variance remains material
retain raw trajectories, ratio/KL/entropy diagnostics, checkpoint hashes and failure slices

algorithms.objective: Clipped policy surrogate with a learned value loss and optional entropy/KL regularization.
algorithms.advantage_or_baseline: GAE or return-minus-learned-value at token or environment-step granularity.
algorithms.long_horizon_credit: Best candidate here when intermediate rewards and environment-step values are trustworthy; final-only reward still leaves sparse credit.
algorithms.zero_variance_behavior: Does not require within-prompt reward variance, but a poor critic or constant returns still removes useful policy signal.
algorithms.compute_memory: HIGH: actor, reference and learned critic plus optimizer states.
algorithms.studyhub_trigger: Run only if GRPO fails specifically because long-horizon value estimation or temporal credit is the missing baseline.
algorithms.studyhub_decision: Do not use as the first 9B run. A PPO comparison must justify the critic labels, memory cost and step-level reward semantics.

algorithms.objective: PPO-style clipped policy optimization using group-relative outcome advantages without a learned critic.
algorithms.advantage_or_baseline: Per-prompt group reward centering and, in the baseline recipe, standardization.
algorithms.long_horizon_credit: Trajectory reward is broadcast to generated action tokens; this is not true temporal credit assignment.
algorithms.zero_variance_behavior: An all-equal group has zero relative advantage and contributes no outcome learning signal.
algorithms.compute_memory: MEDIUM: no critic, but multiple rollouts per prompt dominate inference cost.
algorithms.studyhub_trigger: Default after frozen Benchmark v2, 9B Base calibration, runtime-native SFT, Reward v3 calibration and RL learnability QA pass.
algorithms.studyhub_decision: Use G=4 for the first 500-update main run; use G=8 only in a separate high-branch experiment.

algorithms.objective: Maximize sampled trajectory return with a score-function policy gradient.
algorithms.advantage_or_baseline: Trajectory return minus an optional running, batch or prompt baseline.
algorithms.long_horizon_credit: Final return reaches all actions but has high variance and weak temporal localization.
algorithms.zero_variance_behavior: A batch-normalized implementation loses signal when returns are constant; vanilla uncentered updates can still move but are high variance.
algorithms.studyhub_trigger: Use as a minimal estimator diagnostic when group normalization itself is suspected, not as a substitute for fixing Reward or tasks.

algorithms.objective: Critic-free REINFORCE augmented with PPO-style clipping, normalization and stabilization choices.
algorithms.advantage_or_baseline: Global or batch-normalized return with a running baseline, depending on the exact recipe.
algorithms.long_horizon_credit: Remains trajectory-level unless separate process rewards are supplied.
algorithms.zero_variance_behavior: Global normalization can retain cross-prompt signal that per-prompt GRPO loses, but a constant batch still has no comparative signal.
algorithms.studyhub_trigger: Compare with GRPO when per-prompt zero variance is high but cross-task outcome variation remains informative.
algorithms.studyhub_decision: Conditional; freeze the exact variant because the name covers multiple implementation details.

algorithms.objective: REINFORCE-style optimization using the other samples for the same prompt as a leave-one-out baseline.
algorithms.advantage_or_baseline: Each rollout reward minus the mean reward of the remaining prompt-group rollouts.
algorithms.long_horizon_credit: Sequence-level return remains shared across tokens unless process signals are added.
algorithms.zero_variance_behavior: All-equal prompt groups still have zero advantage; it tests baseline estimation, not task learnability.
algorithms.compute_memory: MEDIUM: no critic, group rollout cost remains.
algorithms.studyhub_trigger: Run if GRPO standardization or estimator bias is suspected while grouped sampling remains affordable.
algorithms.studyhub_decision: Conditional equal-budget diagnostic against the same SFT parent.

algorithms.objective: GRPO-family optimization with decoupled clipping, dynamic sampling, token-level loss aggregation and overlong shaping.
algorithms.advantage_or_baseline: Group-relative reward advantage on dynamically accepted mixed-outcome prompts.
algorithms.long_horizon_credit: Improves length treatment and sample allocation but does not by itself identify which turn caused success.
algorithms.zero_variance_behavior: Filters and resamples all-correct/all-failed groups; this saves updates but may shift the task distribution.
algorithms.studyhub_trigger: Use only if calibration shows material compute loss from zero-variance groups or overlong behavior.
algorithms.studyhub_decision: Conditional component ablation; always report acceptance rate and original-distribution Dev results.

algorithms.objective: Apply importance ratios and clipping at sequence level while retaining group-relative advantages.
algorithms.long_horizon_credit: Sequence-coherent updates improve ratio semantics but remain trajectory-level credit.
algorithms.zero_variance_behavior: All-equal prompt groups still provide no relative outcome advantage.
algorithms.studyhub_trigger: Use when token-level importance ratios have pathological tails or policy staleness harms sequence coherence.
algorithms.studyhub_decision: Conditional after ratio-tail evidence; do not infer benefit from MoE or reasoning results alone.

algorithms.objective: Remove response-length and group-standard-deviation normalizations identified as biased in the analyzed GRPO formulation.
algorithms.advantage_or_baseline: Centered group reward without per-question standard-deviation scaling; fixed rather than response-dependent length normalization.
algorithms.long_horizon_credit: Reduces incentives for unnecessarily long responses; it does not add step-level credit.
algorithms.studyhub_trigger: Only if 9B shows incorrect-response length inflation or reward-scale bias traceable to those normalizers.
algorithms.studyhub_decision: Literature-only until the exact pinned-AReaL loss can be reproduced and a length-bias hypothesis is registered.

algorithms.objective: Clip detached token-level importance weights applied to the policy-gradient loss instead of zeroing gradients with a PPO min surrogate.
algorithms.advantage_or_baseline: Compatible with group-relative or other externally estimated advantages; the MiniMax-M1 recipe uses critic-free RL.
algorithms.long_horizon_credit: Bounds token-ratio variance but does not create temporal credit.
algorithms.zero_variance_behavior: Does not repair a zero advantage estimator.
algorithms.studyhub_trigger: Consider only when clipped-token rate is high and useful gradients are being suppressed despite healthy rewards.
algorithms.studyhub_decision: Literature-only; first confirm implementation support and isolate clipping from other recipe changes.

algorithms.objective: Replace hard clipping with a smooth temperature-controlled gate that is sequence-coherent and token-adaptive.
algorithms.advantage_or_baseline: Group-relative outcome advantage in the published formulation.
algorithms.long_horizon_credit: Preserves more token gradients under ratio outliers but does not add step values.
algorithms.zero_variance_behavior: Does not repair all-equal reward groups.
algorithms.studyhub_trigger: Only if hard clipping suppresses a material share of otherwise useful tokens and GSPO is too coarse.
algorithms.studyhub_decision: Literature-only. This row refers to Qwen's Soft Adaptive Policy Optimization, not other methods sharing the SAPO acronym.

algorithms.objective: Score student-generated tokens with a teacher and minimize reverse KL on student-visited states.
algorithms.advantage_or_baseline: Dense per-token teacher log-probability difference rather than an environment-return baseline.
algorithms.long_horizon_credit: Provides dense token guidance, but teacher errors and teacher-student support mismatch can compound over long trajectories.
algorithms.zero_variance_behavior: Not dependent on group outcome variance; signal vanishes where teacher and student token distributions agree.
algorithms.compute_memory: HIGH: student rollout plus teacher token scoring; rollout-engine teacher is preferred over a train engine.
algorithms.studyhub_trigger: Use only after teacher qualification shows compatible policy structure and incremental capability on student-visited states.
algorithms.studyhub_decision: Conditional retention or capability-transfer experiment, not a replacement for independent outcome evaluation.

algorithms.objective: Combine an online RL objective with reverse-KL teacher distillation on the same student-generated trajectories.
algorithms.advantage_or_baseline: RL advantage plus dense teacher token log-probability guidance.
algorithms.long_horizon_credit: Teacher signal is dense while outcome reward remains trajectory-level; teacher quality becomes part of credit assignment.
algorithms.zero_variance_behavior: The RL branch can lose group signal while the distillation branch still updates, which may preserve behavior or override exploration.
algorithms.compute_memory: VERY_HIGH: online rollout, policy update and teacher scoring.
algorithms.studyhub_trigger: Only with a qualified teacher and a measured need to combine retention or dense guidance with environment outcomes.
algorithms.studyhub_decision: Conditional after GRPO baseline; run weight ablations for RL versus distillation loss and report teacher-student gap.

algorithms.objective: Fit pairwise preferences with a closed-form policy-versus-reference logistic objective.
algorithms.advantage_or_baseline: Chosen versus rejected response pair; no online return estimator.
algorithms.long_horizon_credit: No environment interaction or temporal credit; preference applies to the completed response or trajectory.
algorithms.zero_variance_behavior: Not a group-return issue; duplicate or weak preference pairs provide little signal.
algorithms.compute_memory: MEDIUM: policy and reference scoring, no rollout environment.
algorithms.studyhub_trigger: Use only as an offline preference baseline for response style or frozen trajectories, never as evidence of learned tool policy by itself.
algorithms.studyhub_decision: Offline baseline only; not the 9B Agent RL mainline.

algorithms.objective: Optimize desirable and undesirable examples with a prospect-theoretic utility around a reference KL point.
algorithms.advantage_or_baseline: Binary desirable/undesirable labels; paired responses are not required.
algorithms.long_horizon_credit: No temporal credit or online recovery learning.
algorithms.zero_variance_behavior: Depends on label balance and information, not rollout-group variance.
algorithms.studyhub_trigger: Potential offline baseline if only unpaired good/bad trajectory labels exist.
algorithms.studyhub_decision: Offline baseline only; cannot replace runtime-native Agent RL.

algorithms.objective: Use an identity-link preference objective with a finite target margin to reduce overfitting to deterministic preferences.
algorithms.advantage_or_baseline: Chosen versus rejected pair relative to a fixed reference.
algorithms.long_horizon_credit: No environment-step credit or online exploration.
algorithms.zero_variance_behavior: Not a rollout-group concept; low-quality pairs remain the bottleneck.
algorithms.studyhub_trigger: Only if a controlled offline preference study needs a less aggressively separable DPO-family baseline.
algorithms.studyhub_decision: Literature/offline baseline; not scheduled for the main program.

algorithms.objective: Predict task-level quality or preference for a completed answer or trajectory.
algorithms.advantage_or_baseline: Produces a scalar reward consumed by a policy optimizer; it is not an advantage estimator itself.
algorithms.long_horizon_credit: Sparse terminal signal; cannot localize the responsible turn without additional labels.
algorithms.zero_variance_behavior: A saturated or poorly calibrated RM can create all-equal groups and reward hacking.
algorithms.studyhub_trigger: Use only for rubric dimensions that deterministic end-state checks cannot score, after 500-1000 case calibration.
algorithms.studyhub_decision: Reward v3 component, never the sole evaluator and never shared with Sealed evaluation code.

algorithms.objective: Score intermediate reasoning or Agent steps using step-level correctness or progress supervision.
algorithms.advantage_or_baseline: Produces dense step rewards that a policy optimizer can convert into returns or advantages.
algorithms.long_horizon_credit: Potentially improves temporal localization, provided step labels reflect valid alternative paths rather than one gold trace.
algorithms.zero_variance_behavior: Can add variation to terminally equal outcomes, but a biased process rubric can punish valid exploration.
algorithms.studyhub_trigger: Only after long-horizon failures remain unexplained by environment state and verifiable process diagnostics.
algorithms.studyhub_decision: Component research only; path-agnostic diagnostics precede any learned PRM.
